PLAN "12-Week Resistance Foundation — PCOS Metabolic Health"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Build whole-body strength and improve metabolic health markers"
  GOAL secondary body_composition:
    name "Support insulin sensitivity and lean mass development"

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY insulin_sensitivity
  ANTI_PATTERN under_fuelling

  PRINCIPLES
    PRINCIPLE "Eat enough — chronic restriction raises cortisol, worsens insulin resistance and androgen excess in PCOS"
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise protein at every meal to support muscle protein synthesis and blunt postprandial glucose spikes"
    PRINCIPLE "Anchor carbohydrates around training windows — pre and post workout — to improve glucose disposal"
    PRINCIPLE "Choose low-glycaemic-index carbohydrate sources the majority of the time outside training windows"
    PRINCIPLE "Include dietary fat from whole-food sources to support steroidogenesis and fat-soluble vitamin absorption"
    PRINCIPLE "Distribute meals across 3 to 4 eating occasions per day — avoid skipping meals, especially breakfast"
    PRINCIPLE "Minimise ultra-processed foods, refined sugars and sugar-sweetened beverages"
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise fibre from vegetables, legumes and whole grains to support gut health and glucose regulation"
    PRINCIPLE "Stay well hydrated — target 35 ml per kg bodyweight per day as a baseline"
    PRINCIPLE "Inositol-rich foods such as legumes, citrus and wholegrains complement dietary strategy — discuss supplementation with endocrinologist"

  CALORIES
    BASELINE tdee_maintenance
    ADJUSTMENT none
    RATIONALE "Do not create a caloric deficit. PCOS with irregular cycles and possible HPA dysregulation is worsened by energy restriction. Eat at maintenance or a small surplus on heavy training days."

  MACROS
    protein 1.8..2.2 g_per_kg bodyweight
    carbohydrate 3.5..5.0 g_per_kg bodyweight
    fat 1.0..1.3 g_per_kg bodyweight
    fibre 30..35 g_per_day

  MEAL_TIMING
    MEAL pre_workout 60..90 minutes_before:
      focus "Moderate carbohydrate, moderate protein, low fat, low fibre"
      examples "Oats with whey or Greek yoghurt / rice cakes with cottage cheese / banana with protein shake"
      carbohydrate 30..50 g
      protein 20..30 g
      fat 5..10 g

    MEAL post_workout within_60_minutes:
      focus "High protein, moderate-to-high carbohydrate, low fat"
      examples "Chicken or salmon with rice and roasted vegetables / Greek yoghurt with fruit and granola / protein shake with banana and oat milk"
      carbohydrate 40..60 g
      protein 30..40 g
      fat 5..10 g

    MEAL breakfast daily:
      focus "Protein-led, low-GI carbohydrate, healthy fat — do not skip"
      examples "Eggs with wholegrain toast and avocado / Greek yoghurt parfait with berries and seeds / smoked salmon with oat cakes and spinach"
      carbohydrate 30..50 g
      protein 25..35 g
      fat 10..20 g

    MEAL lunch daily:
      focus "Balanced plate — half vegetables, quarter protein, quarter complex carbohydrate"
      examples "Lentil and vegetable soup with wholegrain bread / grilled chicken salad with quinoa and olive oil dressing / tofu stir-fry with brown rice"
      carbohydrate 40..60 g
      protein 30..40 g
      fat 10..20 g

    MEAL dinner daily:
      focus "Protein and vegetable-forward, moderate carbohydrate, do not restrict"
      examples "Salmon with sweet potato and greens / beef and vegetable stew with barley / chickpea curry with brown rice"
      carbohydrate 40..60 g
      protein 30..40 g
      fat 10..20 g

    MEAL snack optional:
      focus "Protein and fibre anchor — prevents energy crashes and cortisol spikes between meals"
      examples "Apple with almond butter / cottage cheese with cucumber / hard-boiled eggs with oat cakes / edamame"
      carbohydrate 10..20 g
      protein 10..20 g
      fat 5..10 g

  FOODS
    PRIORITISE
      "Lean proteins — chicken, turkey, salmon, sardines, eggs, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tofu, tempeh, legumes"
      "Complex carbohydrates — oats, brown rice, quinoa, sweet potato, barley, wholegrain bread, lentils, chickpeas"
      "Non-starchy vegetables — broccoli, spinach, kale, courgette, peppers, cucumber, asparagus, cauliflower"
      "Healthy fats — avocado, olive oil, nuts, seeds, oily fish, nut butters"
      "High-fibre foods — legumes, berries, flaxseed, chia seeds, wholegrains, brassicas"
      "Anti-inflammatory foods — oily fish, walnuts, turmeric, ginger, berries, dark leafy greens"

    LIMIT
      "Refined carbohydrates — white bread, pastries, sugary cereals, white rice in large portions outside training"
      "Sugar-sweetened beverages — soft drinks, fruit juice, energy drinks, sweetened coffee drinks"
      "Ultra-processed foods — packaged snacks, fast food, processed meats"
      "Alcohol — disrupts sleep, raises cortisol, impairs glucose regulation"
      "High-GI foods in isolation — especially outside training windows"

  SUPPLEMENTS
    SUPPLEMENT "Vitamin D3 + K2":
      rationale "Highly prevalent deficiency in PCOS — supports insulin signalling and ovarian function"

PLAN "Flare Management Protocol — PCOS Irregular Cycle"
TYPE guidance
VISIBILITY public

PROTOCOL flare_management

  RATIONALE
    "This client has no reliable cycle to predict flare windows. Flares may be driven by oestrogen fluctuation, prostaglandin activity, systemic inflammation, or HPA dysregulation — all common in PCOS. Until cycle regularity improves, flares must be managed reactively rather than proactively. The protocol below gives the trainer a decision tree to apply whenever a flare is reported."

  SEVERITY_CLASSIFICATION
    LEVEL 1 mild:
      definition "Discomfort present but does not limit daily movement. Pain score 1..3 out of 10. No referred pain. Client can walk normally."
      training_modification "Reduce load by 20 percent. Omit high-axial-load movements. Keep session duration. Monitor within session."

    LEVEL 2 moderate:
      definition "Pain limits some daily activities. Pain score 4..6 out of 10. Possible lower back or pelvic referral. Standing for extended periods uncomfortable."
      training_modification "Replace resistance session with mobility and breathwork only. Cardio reduced to flat walking at RPE 3..4, 15..20 minutes maximum. No axial loading. No spinal flexion under load."

    LEVEL 3 severe:
      definition "Pain significantly limits daily function. Pain score 7..10 out of 10. Referred pain into legs or upper back. Client cannot sit or stand comfortably for more than a few minutes."
      training_modification "Full rest. No structured exercise. Encourage gentle walking around home only if tolerated. Refer back to endocrinologist if severity is new or worsening."

  DECISION_TREE
    STEP 1 "Client reports flare":
      action "Classify severity using levels above. Ask: pain score, location, referred symptoms, impact on daily movement."

    STEP 2 "Determine flare day within training week":
      action "If flare begins on or before a resistance day — replace that session per severity level. If flare begins after a resistance day already completed — assess whether next session needs modification."

    STEP 3 "Apply session substitutions":
      SUBSTITUTION axial_load_movements:
        remove "squat, deadlift, romanian_deadlift, front_squat, goblet_squat, split_squat, leg_press, good_morning, barbell_row, bent_over_row"
        replace_with "glute_bridge, hip_thrust, leg_curl, leg_extension, seated_calf_raise, lat_pulldown, seated_row, bench_press, shoulder_press, face_pull, lateral_raise"
        rationale "All replacements are supine, seated or bench-supported. Zero compressive lumbar load."

      SUBSTITUTION cardio:
        remove "rowing, running, elliptical at high resistance"
        replace_with "walking, cycling at low resistance and upright position"
        rationale "Rowing and running create repetitive lumbar loading. Upright cycling and flat walking are tolerable during moderate flares."

      SUBSTITUTION core:
        remove "plank, side_plank, ab_wheel, hanging_leg_raise, russian_twist, sit_up, crunch"
        replace_with "dead_bug, bird_dog, glute_bridge, diaphragmatic_breathing, cat_cow, child_pose, pelvic_tilt"
        rationale "Avoid spinal flexion and isometric bracing under pain. Anti-extension and breathing-based work is safe and actively reduces cortisol."

    STEP 4 "Monitor flare duration":
      action "Log flare start and end date every occurrence. Note cycle day if menstruation is present. Over time this data may reveal a pattern even within an irregular cycle."
      tool "Simple log — date, pain score, cycle day if known, sessions modified, sessions missed."

    STEP 5 "Return to training":
      criteria "Pain score returned to 0..2. Client can perform daily activities without limitation. At least one full rest day after last symptomatic day before resuming normal loading."
      action "Return at the load level from two sessions prior — not the session immediately before the flare. Do not attempt to make up missed volume."
      rationale "Returning too aggressively after a flare is the most common error. Undertrained is recoverable. Re-injured is not."

  NUTRITION_DURING_FLARE
    PRINCIPLE "Do not restrict calories during a flare. Tissue repair and immune response increase energy demand."
    PRINCIPLE "Increase anti-inflammatory foods — oily fish, walnuts, turmeric, ginger, dark berries, leafy greens."
    PRINCIPLE "Maintain protein intake at programme targets — muscle catabolism accelerates during pain-related inactivity."
    PRINCIPLE "Magnesium glycinate dose can be maintained or increased to upper range during flare — supports pain modulation and sleep."
    PRINCIPLE "Avoid alcohol entirely during flare — raises prostaglandin activity and worsens inflammation."
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise hydration — dehydration lowers pain threshold."

  COMMUNICATION_GUIDELINES
    GUIDELINE "Establish a simple check-in system — client messages trainer at flare onset with pain score and location. No need for full assessment every time once protocol is familiar."
    GUIDELINE "Normalise flare occurrence — this is a feature of the condition, not a failure of the programme or the client."
    GUIDELINE "Never frame missed sessions as something to compensate for. The programme absorbs flares by design."
    GUIDELINE "If flares are occurring more than twice per 8-week block, escalate to endocrinologist — programme stimulus may be exceeding recovery capacity, or the condition may need medical review."
    GUIDELINE "Track flare data alongside training data. Present patterns to endocrinologist at next appointment."

  RED_FLAGS
    FLAG "Flare severity increasing over successive occurrences — refer to endocrinologist before next session"
    FLAG "Flare duration extending beyond 7 days — do not continue programme, seek medical review"
    FLAG "New neurological symptoms — leg numbness, tingling, bladder or bowel changes — cease all exercise and refer urgently"
    FLAG "Flare accompanied by fever — this is not a typical PCOS flare, seek medical attention"
    FLAG "Client reporting low mood, hopelessness or disordered eating during or after flares — refer to appropriate psychological support"
